summary: There is no way to edit an existing catalog entry's metadata while retaining its identity and per-field provenance; the only editable path (CustomDialog) always creates a brand-new, provenance-flattened record, and the persisted schema has no per-field provenance column at all despite `FieldValue<T>`/`Provenance.CATALOG_EDITED` being modeled in core.
claim: There is no way to edit an existing catalog entry's metadata while retaining its identity and per-field provenance; the only editable path (CustomDialog) always creates a brand-new, provenance-flattened record, and the persisted schema has no per-field provenance column at all despite `FieldValue<T>`/`Provenance.CATALOG_EDITED` being modeled in core.

evidence.source: Detail composable (MainActivity.kt) only displays catalog fields read-only (Info(...) calls); the sole editable UI, CustomDialog, is reached only via the blank 'Custom filament' FAB or via decodedSeed(), and MainViewModel.saveCustom() always assigns `UUID.randomUUID()` as packageId and `Provenance.CUSTOM`. `Provenance.CATALOG_EDITED` (core/Filament.kt) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the app source. CustomRecord (data/Databases.kt) stores plain String/Int fields, not `FieldValue<T>`, so no per-field source is persisted even for the records that do exist.

suggested_remediation: Implement an actual catalog-entry edit flow that writes a `CATALOG_EDITED` record keyed to the original packageId, persisting a source tag per field (or per-record 'edited' status) that survives catalog reinstall/replacement.
suggested_validation: Edit one field of a catalog entry, kill the process, force a catalog replacement (digest/count mismatch path in ensureCatalog()), relaunch, and confirm the edited field is retained with 'edited' provenance while untouched fields still show 'OFD <revision>'.
